extension.name: com.kinetica.nifi.processors.GetKineticaToCSV
extension.description: Monitors a Kinetica table for new records and outputs them as CSV files. Uses ZeroMQ table monitor for real-time notifications. The output includes a header row with column names and types in Kinetica schema format.

property.name: Server URL
property.description: URL of the Kinetica server. Example: http://172.3.4.19:9191

property.name: Table Name
property.description: Name of the Kinetica table. Can include schema prefix (e.g., 'schema.table_name').

property.name: Username
property.description: Username for Kinetica authentication. Leave empty if authentication is not required.

property.name: Password
property.description: Password for Kinetica authentication.

property.name: Table Monitor URL
property.description: URL of the Kinetica table monitor endpoint for ZeroMQ subscriptions. Example: tcp://172.3.4.19:9002

property.name: Delimiter
property.description: Field delimiter for CSV output. Default is tab character.

relationship.name: success
relationship.description: FlowFiles containing data read from Kinetica

extension.name: com.kinetica.nifi.processors.PutKinetica
extension.description: Bulk loads FlowFile attributes to Kinetica in batch intervals. Each FlowFile must contain attributes that match your schema definition. Example: Given schema 'x|Float|data,y|Float|data,TEXT|String|data', this processor expects attributes named x, y, and TEXT in each FlowFile. Set Batch Size appropriately for your throughput needs (e.g., 10K records/sec requires batch size ~10000).

property.name: Server URL
property.description: URL of the Kinetica server. Example: http://172.3.4.19:9191

property.name: Table Name
property.description: Name of the Kinetica table. Can include schema prefix (e.g., 'schema.table_name').

property.name: Username
property.description: Username for Kinetica authentication. Leave empty if authentication is not required.

property.name: Password
property.description: Password for Kinetica authentication.

property.name: Collection Name
property.description: Name of the Kinetica collection (optional). Tables can be organized into collections.

property.name: Schema
property.description: Schema of the Kinetica table. Required if table doesn't exist. Format: column1|type|annotations,column2|type|annotations,... Example: x|Float|data,y|Float|data,TIMESTAMP|Long|data,TEXT|String|store_only|text_search

property.name: Batch Size
property.description: Number of records to batch before flushing to Kinetica. Higher values improve throughput but use more memory.

property.name: Update on Existing PK
property.description: If true and the table has a primary key, existing records with matching keys will be updated. If false, records with existing keys are ignored.

property.name: Replicate Table
property.description: If true and table needs to be created, the table will be replicated across all cluster nodes.

property.name: Date Format
property.description: Date format pattern for parsing datetime values. Example: yyyy/MM/dd HH:mm:ss

property.name: Timezone
property.description: Timezone for datetime values. If not set, the system default will be used. Example: EST, UTC

relationship.name: success
relationship.description: FlowFiles that were successfully written to Kinetica

relationship.name: failure
relationship.description: FlowFiles that failed to be written to Kinetica

readsAttribute.description: Reads all FlowFile attributes that match the table column names

extension.name: com.kinetica.nifi.processors.PutKineticaFromFile
extension.description: Bulk loads delimited file contents (CSV, TSV, etc.) to Kinetica. Each file must contain columns matching the schema definition in the same order. Example: For schema 'x|Float|data,y|Float|data,TEXT|String|data', the file should have columns x, y, TEXT in that order. The processor ignores header rows by default. For best performance, chunk large files into ~1M rows.

property.name: Server URL
property.description: URL of the Kinetica server. Example: http://172.3.4.19:9191

property.name: Table Name
property.description: Name of the Kinetica table. Can include schema prefix (e.g., 'schema.table_name').

property.name: Username
property.description: Username for Kinetica authentication. Leave empty if authentication is not required.

property.name: Password
property.description: Password for Kinetica authentication.

property.name: Collection Name
property.description: Name of the Kinetica collection (optional). Tables can be organized into collections.

property.name: Schema
property.description: Schema of the Kinetica table. Required if table doesn't exist. Format: column1|type|annotations,column2|type|annotations,... Example: x|Float|data,y|Float|data,TIMESTAMP|Long|data,TEXT|String|store_only|text_search

property.name: Batch Size
property.description: Number of records to batch before flushing to Kinetica. Higher values improve throughput but use more memory.

property.name: Update on Existing PK
property.description: If true and the table has a primary key, existing records with matching keys will be updated. If false, records with existing keys are ignored.

property.name: Replicate Table
property.description: If true and table needs to be created, the table will be replicated across all cluster nodes.

property.name: Date Format
property.description: Date format pattern for parsing datetime values. Example: yyyy/MM/dd HH:mm:ss

property.name: Timezone
property.description: Timezone for datetime values. If not set, the system default will be used. Example: EST, UTC

property.name: Delimiter
property.description: Field delimiter character. Common values: ',' (comma), '\t' (tab), '|' (pipe)

property.name: Escape Character
property.description: Escape character for special characters. Default is double-quote '"'

property.name: Quote Character
property.description: Quote character for fields containing special characters. Set to empty string to disable quoting.

property.name: File Has Header
property.description: If true, the first row is treated as a header and skipped. The header is preserved in the failure output for bad records.

property.name: Skip Errors
property.description: If true, invalid records are skipped and processing continues. If false, the entire file fails on the first error.

relationship.name: success
relationship.description: FlowFiles that were successfully written to Kinetica

relationship.name: failure
relationship.description: FlowFiles that failed to be written to Kinetica
